title: Agroforestry for landscape restoration
claim: Integrating trees and shrubs into cropland through agroforestry improves water infiltration and soil moisture retention while adding structural habitat that can connect otherwise isolated patches of vegetation.
evidence_text: FAO's landscape restoration guidance describes agroforestry systems — trees integrated into cropland as rows, boundaries, or scattered cover — as a practice that increases root-zone water infiltration, reduces evapotranspiration losses, and builds soil organic matter over time. The added vertical vegetation structure also provides stepping-stone habitat that can partially reconnect fragmented natural areas within agricultural landscapes.
